claims.text: Excess Zr powder will act as an in-situ oxygen getter during hydride decomposition in argon.
Zr scavenging will remove oxygen released during hydride decomposition.
Oxygen scavenging by Zr will prevent nucleation of alpha-HCP phases.
Rapid quenching after getter-assisted processing will retain a metastable single-phase beta-BCC structure.
Retention of beta-BCC requires a heating rate exceeding the critical dehydrogenation rate of the hydrides.
The precursor has an equiatomic Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr elemental composition and contains metallic and hydride powders.
Adding 5-10 wt% excess Zr is an effective getter dosage for this feedstock.
A heating rate greater than 50 K/min is sufficient to balance dehydrogenation and oxygen scavenging.
Processing under argon with an oxygen partial pressure below 1 ppm is required.
Rapid quenching from above 1200 degrees Celsius will trap the high-temperature beta-BCC phase.
Scavenged oxygen reacts with excess Zr to form ZrO2 in situ.
Formation of ZrO2 prevents oxygen from dissolving into the metallic matrix.
The oxygen affinity and formation enthalpy of ZrO2 allow Zr oxidation to outcompete oxygen-induced stabilization of alpha-HCP phases.
Rapid dehydrogenation prevents oxygen accumulation in a molten phase.
The proposed regime will produce a nearly fully dense microstructure.
The quenched microstructure will be single-phase metastable beta-BCC with grain size below 50 micrometers.
No alpha-HCP or alpha-Ti phase will be detectable after quenching.
Sintering without a getter, or with Ti alone, causes oxygen dissolution and alpha-phase formation.
Slow heating allows oxygen to diffuse into the lattice despite the presence of the Zr getter.

contradictions.description: The feedstock is described as equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, but adding 5-10 wt% excess Zr makes the overall precursor non-equiatomic unless the oxidized excess is subsequently removed or explicitly excluded from the alloy composition.
The intervention specifies a heating rate greater than 50 K/min, whereas the proposed experiment uses exactly 50 K/min and therefore does not directly test the stated regime.
